title: A descended coproduct model represents the original pro-etale sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $p:V\to X$ be weakly étale, flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and assume $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $S$ be any set in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], put $T=\coprod_{s\in S}V$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose natural bijections $a_W:F(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_V(W,T)$ are given for all weakly étale $W\to V$. Let $\delta:p_1^*T\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^*T$ be a descent datum over $R=V\times_XV$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pd-descent-datum] inducing, through these bijections, the canonical comparison between the two restrictions of $F|_V$. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a scheme with an isomorphism $\eta:Y\times_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ over $V$ inducing $\delta$.

Then $q$ is separated and étale [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism], and is surjective if $S$ is nonempty. There are unique natural bijections $b_U:F(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,Y)$ for all $U\to X$ in $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ whose restriction to $U_V=U\times_XV$, followed by $\eta$, agrees with $a_{U_V}$. Equivalently the local map $a_{U_V}(s|_{U_V})$ descends to $b_U(s)$, and the inverse bijection descends the local section associated to a pulled-back map $U\to Y$. The étale scheme $Y$ is itself an object of the pro-étale site, and $u=b_Y^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_Y)\in F(Y)$ has $b_U(F(f)(u))=f$ for every $X$-morphism $f:U\to Y$ from a site object. On $T$, this universal section corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_T$ under $a_T$. Empty $S$ and empty $X$ are allowed (surjectivity is asserted only under the stated nonemptiness assumption).

proof.text: The codiagonal t is etale by Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc applied to identity maps, including the empty family. For separatedness, form blocks V -> T ×_V T with projections j_i,j_k. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_map identifies their ranges with the intersections of the two inverse images of component ranges. Their union for i != k is open. The component cover and disjointness identify that union with the complement of the diagonal range. Thus the diagonal range is closed; the diagonal is a preimmersion, so IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion proves t separated.

proof.text: Transfer separatedness and etaleness across eta to the pullback of q. Apply isSeparated_of_flat_surjective_baseChange and etale_of_fpqc_cover for the singleton family p. A chosen index of nonempty S supplies a morphism V -> Y above p, hence q is surjective. Mathlib etale_le_weaklyEtale supplies the site witnesses.

proof.text: The object p covers the terminal object of the small pro-etale site: for each U, the projection U ×_X V -> U is weakly etale, flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and its singleton is a covering presieve. Use Mathlib singleton_mem_propQCPrecoverage and generate_mem_toGrothendieck. Weakly etale cancellation makes every lift W -> V of a site object an object over V. The presheaf Hom_X(-,Y) is a sheaf by subcanonicity of the pro-etale topology and continuity of ProEt.forget.

proof.text: For a site object W with a lift f to V, identify F(W) with Hom_V(W,T) by a, composing with the identity-underlying comparison of site objects; then compose with eta inverse and the map/pullback adjunction to obtain a bijection to Hom_X(W,Y). The equations hdelta and heta imply independence from f; naturality ha gives compatibility with every restriction, even with a different lift at its source.

source.place: (2)-(3); Stacks 02KU, 02VN and 023Q; Mathlib sheaf amalgamation API

proof.text: The proved private helper localEquivalences glues these bijections on the covering sieve of arrows whose sources map to V. For a section of either sheaf, use each local bijection (or its inverse) after restriction to define a matching family. Compatibility follows from the preceding restriction identity. Amalgamate with the sheaf axiom. Both round trips and naturality follow by separatedness on this covering sieve. Hence obtain natural equivalences b agreeing with the specified local formula at every lift.

source.place: (2)-(3); Stacks 02KU, 02VN and 023Q; Mathlib sheaf amalgamation API

proof.text: On C=U ×_X V, apply the local formula at its second projection and naturality at its first projection. The pullback universal property and eta invertibility give exactly the required normalization. For u=b_Y inverse(id), naturality gives b_U(F(f)u)=f. Apply the local formula to T with its structure lift and the morphism eta inverse followed by the first projection; the pullback universal property gives a_T(F(r)u)=id_T. Finally, any other normalized family has the same maps after the flat, surjective, quasi-compact projection C -> U; this is an effective epi, hence an epi, so the families agree. All these steps allow empty bases and empty S; choosing an index was used only for conditional surjectivity.
